name: Baserow 2.4 No-Code Database (Postgres, Redis, Celery, S3)
idSeed: Baserow 2.4 No-Code Database (Postgres, Redis, Celery, S3)
description: Open-source Airtable alternative: API, Celery workers and Bucket files.

PORT.description: Port of the gateway (public domain target and healthcheck).

PRIVATE_WEB_FRONTEND_URL.description: Web frontend on the private network (everything else).

BASEROW_BACKEND_BIND_ADDRESS.description: Listen on IPv4 and IPv6 (Railway private network).

BASEROW_PUBLIC_URL.description: Public URL of Baserow (the Baserow gateway service). Change it when you add a custom domain, here only; the other services reference it.

PRIVATE_BACKEND_URL.description: Backend URL on the private network (used by the frontend, the gateway and internal tools).

BASEROW_EXTRA_ALLOWED_HOSTS.description: Extra Host headers Django accepts: the private name and Railway's healthcheck.

SECRET_KEY.description: Django secret key, shared with the Celery services. Keep it stable.

BASEROW_JWT_SIGNING_KEY.description: Signs login tokens. Changing it signs everyone out.

DATABASE_URL.description: PostgreSQL connection over the private network (pgvector is enabled automatically).

REDIS_URL.description: Redis for cache, realtime updates and the Celery queues.

BASEROW_OSS_ONLY.description: true = load only the MIT-licensed open-source edition (no premium/enterprise code). Empty = load them too; they need a paid Baserow licence.

BASEROW_AMOUNT_OF_WORKERS.description: Celery concurrency per worker service (default would follow the host's CPU count).

BASEROW_ENABLE_SECURE_PROXY_SSL_HEADER.description: Trust X-Forwarded-Proto from Railway's HTTPS edge.

BASEROW_POSTGRES_STARTUP_CHECK_ATTEMPTS.description: Postgres connection attempts on start (Postgres may still be starting).

BASEROW_ADMIN_EMAIL.description: E-mail (login) of the first admin, created on the first start before the API listens. Change it later in account settings.

BASEROW_ADMIN_PASSWORD.description: Password of the first admin (8-256 chars). Generated; read it here to log in.

BASEROW_ADMIN_NAME.description: Display name of the first admin.

BASEROW_ADMIN_RESET_PASSWORD.description: true = on the next start, set the password of BASEROW_ADMIN_EMAIL to BASEROW_ADMIN_PASSWORD. Set back to false afterwards.

BASEROW_ALLOW_NEW_SIGNUPS.description: Applied once at the first start: false = only invited people can sign up. Change later in Admin > Settings.

AWS_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME.description: Railway Bucket for uploaded files, thumbnails and exports (shared by the backend and the Celery workers).

AWS_S3_SIGNATURE_VERSION.description: Signature version for signed file URLs.

AWS_DEFAULT_ACL.description: Files stay private; browsers get signed URLs.

AWS_QUERYSTRING_AUTH.description: Serve files through signed, expiring URLs.

AWS_QUERYSTRING_EXPIRE.description: Lifetime of signed file URLs in seconds (1 day).

BASEROW_BUCKET_CORS.description: Set the Bucket CORS rule for BASEROW_PUBLIC_URL on each start (file previews in the browser). false = leave it alone.

EMAIL_SMTP.description: Optional: set to true to send e-mail (invitations, password resets, notifications) through SMTP. Outbound SMTP needs Railway Pro.

NITRO_PORT.description: Port the Nuxt server listens on.

NITRO_HOST.description: Listen on IPv4 and IPv6 (Railway private network).
